name: CR-Int-16-trigonometric-6
questiontext: Find \[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}}. \] Hint: square an identity for \(\cos^2(A)\). [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: For this question we need to use the identity \[cos^2(A) = \frac{1}{2}[1+cos(2A)]\] as follows: \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle [{{CT:2}}]^2\\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \left[{{CT:3}}\right]^2 \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:4}} \end{array}\] So, \[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} = \int {{CT:4}} d{{CT:1}} \] To solve this integral we need to express \[{{CT:5}}\] in a simpler form using the same identity: \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:5}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}}{{CT:7}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}}\left[{{CT:8}}\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:9}} \end{array}\] Hence, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:9}} + {{CT:10}} + {{CT:6}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:11}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:12}} \end{array}\]
